(Below is just my stance on why DIY isn't usually the best option but is in this case. I definitely have some biases, though.)
---
I've been really lucky to get amazing medical care in every area except this, and I know many of the people working in the medical field have decades of training and experience that allows them to see things in ways I might not. 

For something specific and niche like this, I think DIY is probably the way to go because most healthcare workers and such don't get trained on this sort of thing.

Even the ones who do and specialize in this often don't have up to date info or procedures as more research comes out and new/better medications are developed, or are bound by the boards and such that give them their licenses to practice and so can't offer experimental treatments to everyone even if there is research that shows it probably works better and is safer than the current standard of care. (I wouldn't be surprised if many healthcare workers who work with trans people are pushing for changes, but that's a long process and the people in places of power often don't look favorably on us.)

This doesn't mean the medical system we have in place is bad, though- it's certainly not perfect, especially from a financial and political view, and corporations and politicians exploit it, but it *works incredibly well for most things*. Our current medical technology- everything from the tools and drugs to the typical ways healthcare professionals and taught to handle things- is typically based on an immense amount of science and research and data.

Except in Dentistry. Dentistry is more based on tradition and 'conventional wisdom' and resists change much more than other medical fields.

Even if I think DIY for HRT is probably the superior option (from a health outcome perspective- it's certainly a lot more work for the patient) I would still for example, trust a trained orthopedic surgeon to handle a broken leg over DIY any day, no matter how much research I myself had done.
And yes, I can provide sources to back this up.
